newsitem.title: GERMANY: Colonia aims for increased Postbank share.
newsitem.headline: Colonia aims for increased Postbank share.

text.p: German insurance group Colonia AG said on Friday it wanted to increase its share of Postbank AG to 15 percent as part of a proposal to sell financial products through the country's vast post office network.
But the proposal, published after talks with Post Ministry officials, drew immediate criticism from state-controlled Postbank -- which is slated for further privatisation.

Colonia board member Carl Hermann Schleiffer told Reuters that its plan to increase its stake from 10 percent would generate sales volume of three billion marks ($2 billion) by 2005 -- guaranteeing 300 million marks for Postbank and Deutsche Post.
Postbank, which has exclusive rights to sell financial services at Germany's 16,500 post offices, reacted by criticizing Colonia, saying the it should choose its own partner, not the ministry.
"It is inexplicable why Colonia would go to the ministry with its proposal," a Postbank spokesman said.
Colonia, Germany's third-largest insurer, is 75 percent owned by France insurance company UAP.
